# Resizable pins a resize to its start size when the boundary is no ancestor

## Context

Leaf of #21061. Julia's review of #21073 asked for the web desktop's windows to resize inside the workspace, the area above the taskbar, through `resizablePluginConfig: {boundaryContainerId: workspaceId}`. With that config a window cannot be resized at all.

## The Problem

A real-browser control in Chromium, on the web desktop at 1280 × 800, with the workspace bottom at 740. A window spans 210–590, and its bottom edge is dragged to 790:

| Config | Bottom after the drag |
|---|---|
| none (`boundaryContainerId: 'document.body'`) | 790, over the taskbar |
| `resizablePluginConfig: {boundaryContainerId: workspaceId}` | 590, unchanged: the resize is pinned to its start size |
| the same config, with the fix below | 740, stopped at the workspace |

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.plugin.Resizable#onDragStart` (`src/plugin/Resizable.mjs`) looks for the boundary container on the dragged element's event path, "assuming that the dragEl is not outside of the container".
- A dialog renders on the document body, so a workspace container is never on its path. The fallback then calls `owner.getDomRect(me.boundaryContainerRect)` with that rect still `null`. The measured box is not the container, and the drag is clamped to it.
- `onDragEnd` resets `boundaryContainerRect`, so each drag measures afresh; only the fallback's argument is wrong.
- Design authority: n/a. The defect excuse is the browser control above; the member's JSDoc is a bare `@member` with no description.

## The Fix

The fallback measures the container by its id: `owner.getDomRect(containerId)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A boundary container that is not on the dragged element's path is measured by its id (unit, red on `dev`).
- [ ] An ancestor container is still read from the event path, with no extra measuring (unit).
- [ ] In the web desktop, a window's resize stops at the workspace (browser witness, #21073's branch).

## Out of Scope

- Rect timing: the fallback measures asynchronously, so the first moves of a drag may run before the rect arrives. That is unchanged.

## Related

- Parent: #21061. Found by the review of #21073 (Resolves #21064), which carries the fix.
